content.subject: Urgent: open invoice no. 2026-1147 – reminder
content.body_md:
Dear Sir or Madam,

unfortunately we have not yet received your payment. Please settle the amount **within 24 hours** to avoid late fees.

You will find the invoice attached.

Kind regards
Accounts

red_flags.hint: The domain says "logistlk" instead of "logistik": one letter is swapped.
Artificial urgency: you are meant to act before you think.
Double extension: this is an .exe, a program, not a PDF.

explanation: Fake invoice. An .exe attachment is never an invoice. Check with the supplier on their known phone number and tap "Report".

content.subject: Confidential – quick request
content.body_md:
Hello,

I am about to go into a meeting with the notary and cannot be reached. For an acquisition, a down payment of €48,500 has to go out today. I will send the account details shortly.

Please treat this as strictly confidential and do not talk to anyone about it, not even in your department.

S. Müller

red_flags.hint: Management does not write from a free mail account. The display name proves nothing.
Being unreachable stops you from checking back.
Secrecy is meant to bypass the four-eyes principle.

explanation: CEO fraud. Authority + urgency + secrecy is the classic pattern. Check back through a known channel; payments always follow the four-eyes principle.

content.subject: Your password expires today
content.body_md:
Dear user,

your password expires in 3 hours. After that your mailbox will be locked and all emails will be lost.

Keep your current password now:

red_flags.hint: This is neither your company domain nor the real OfficeCloud domain.
A generic greeting: your own IT knows your name.
Fear of loss is a strong lever and here completely unrealistic.
Long-press the link: it leads to a foreign domain.

explanation: Password phishing. Only change passwords through the known portal, never through a link in an email.

content.subject: Julia Brandt shared "Offer_Q4_final.pdf" with you
content.body_md:
Julia Brandt shared a document with you.

Note: sign in with your company password to view the document.

red_flags.hint: A third-party service never needs your company password. That is exactly what the attackers want.
You do not know any Julia Brandt and expect no offer. Unexpected means: check first.

explanation: Real service, wrong intent: the link really is on DataBox, the file behind it is the trap. That is why a clean sender does not help here. Ask the person another way.

content.subject: Bonus payout 2026 – please review
content.body_md:
Dear colleagues,

attached is the list of bonus payments. To display the amounts, please click "Enable content" when opening the file.

red_flags.hint: Nearly right: .test instead of .example. Your real domain is muster-automotive.example.
.xlsm means Excel with macros, and macros are program code.
"Enable content" starts the macros. That is the classic trap.

explanation: Macro attachment baited with "salaries". Curiosity is the lever. Nobody sends real salary data as a list to everyone.

content.subject: Change of our bank details
content.body_md:
Hello,

because we are switching banks, please transfer open and future invoices to the following account effective immediately:

IBAN DE00 1234 5678 9012 3456 78

Please confirm briefly by replying to this email.

Kind regards
Petra Vogel

red_flags.hint: The real domain is kessler-stahl.example. Here "-gmbh" was added and the ending changed.
Changed bank details are the heart of this fraud. Always verify them by phone.
The confirmation is meant to stay in the fraudster's channel. Call the known number instead.

explanation: Invoice fraud (BEC). No attachment, no link, no typo: that is why it is dangerous. Always verify bank changes via the known phone number, never using details from the email.

content.subject: STRICTLY CONFIDENTIAL BUSINESS 14.5 MILLION USD
content.body_md:
Dear friend,

I am the lawyer of a deceased client. You will receive 30% of 14.5 million dollars if you help me transfer the money. Just send your bank details and a small handling fee.

red_flags.hint: Too good to be true. It is.
Advance-fee fraud: you pay small fees for money that never exists.

explanation: The classic. Hardly anyone falls for it any more, but it shows the principle: exploiting greed.

content.subject: RE: RE: Delivery of switch cabinets week 46
content.body_md:
Hello,

as just discussed, the updated invoice for the delivery. The attachment is encrypted for data protection reasons, the password is: 4471.

> On 28 Oct you wrote: Please confirm the delivery date for week 46.

red_flags.hint: No virus scanner can inspect a password-protected archive. That is exactly why it is used.
The invoice normally comes as a PDF. A sudden change is a warning sign.
There was no conversation. Mr Thiel's account was hijacked; the thread is real.

explanation: Thread hijacking: the sender and the thread are real, the account was taken over. If the details fit but the behaviour does not, make a quick call. This trick made Emotet so successful.

content.subject: Quick question about the login details
content.body_md: Hi, I cannot get into the supplier portal right now. Could you quickly send me your password? It is really urgent, the meeting is in ten minutes.

red_flags.hint: Look closely: "autornotive". The "m" became "rn". In many fonts these look the same.
Passwords are never shared, not even among colleagues. That is always a warning sign.

explanation: Homoglyph domain: "rn" looks like "m". Never pass on passwords, no matter who asks.

content.subject: Your tax refund: €468.23
content.body_md:
Dear customer,

you are entitled to a refund. Enter your card details within 48 hours so that we can transfer the amount.

red_flags.hint: The tax office never asks for card details by email and does not call you a "customer".
Authorities do not use a domain like this.
The link does not lead to an authority.

explanation: Greed and authority: money from the tax office. Authorities write by post or through their official portal.

content.subject: Lunch on Friday?
content.body_md:
Hi all,

we would like to go to the canteen together on Friday at 12:30. Who is in? Just drop me a line.

Cheers, Lena

explanation: Genuine: internal address, no link, no attachment, no pressure. Not everything is an attack.

content.subject: Invoice 88213 for your order 4500127
content.body_md:
Hello Ms Schneider,

please find attached the invoice for your order 4500127 of 21 Oct. Payment is due in 30 days as agreed; the bank details are unchanged.

Kind regards
Kessler Stahl GmbH, Accounts

explanation: Genuine invoice: known domain, your order number, your name, a normal PDF, no pressure. Right to process it.

content.subject: Maintenance on Saturday, 8 to 12
content.body_md:
Hi all,

on Saturday the ERP system will be unavailable from 8 to 12. You do not need to do anything. The service team answers questions on extension 400.

explanation: Genuine info: internal address, nothing asked of you, no link. Nothing speaks against it.

content.subject: Your payslip is ready
content.body_md:
Hello,

as every month, your October payslip is ready in the HR portal. You can find it as usual through your bookmark on the intranet.

explanation: Genuine: the message has no link and sends you to the portal your usual way. This is what good emails look like.

content.subject: Reminder: fire safety training by 30 Nov
content.body_md:
Hello,

please complete the annual fire safety training by 30 Nov. It takes about 15 minutes.

explanation: Genuine: internal domain, the link stays on your domain as well, the deadline is realistic.

content.subject: Your password reset link
content.body_md: You just clicked "Forgot password" (1 minute ago, from your location Zwickau). If this was not you, ignore this email.

explanation: Genuine, because you just requested it yourself: expected + right domain + no pressure. The decisive factor is that YOU started the process.

content.subject: Order confirmation no. 20419
content.body_md:
Hello Helga,

thank you for your order from yesterday: "The Garden in Autumn", €18.90. You chose to pay by invoice, the book will arrive in 2 to 3 days.

explanation: Genuine: you really did order, the order is correct, nobody wants data or a click from you.

content.subject: Plant news: new canteen from January
content.body_md: From January, the new canteen opens in hall 3. As always, the menu will be posted at the entrance.

explanation: Genuine: just information, no action required.

content.subject: New payslip portal: confirm your access by Friday
content.body_md:
Good morning,

from December we are moving payslips to the new portal. You will find the instructions attached.

Please confirm your access by Friday so that your next payslip reaches you on time.

Kind regards
Your HR team

pdf.title: Moving to the payslip portal
lines: for security reasons, signing in to the new portal is now only possible from your smartphone.
Scan the code below with your phone camera and sign in with your company account.

red_flags.hint: The company uses muster-automotive.example. "-hr.test" is a foreign domain that only looks as if it belonged.
A QR code in the PDF moves you away from the protected company computer: mail filters and link checks no longer apply there.

explanation: Quishing by PDF: the code hides the destination from filters and from you. The letter is flawless and calm. Only the sender domain and the detour through your phone give it away.

content.subject: RE: Framework agreement 2027 – draft for review
content.body_md:
Hello,

as discussed, please find the draft framework agreement attached. Could you have a quick look before our meeting, section 4 in particular.

Best regards
Daniel Roth
Kessler Stahl GmbH

pdf.title: This document is encrypted
lines: The sender has protected this PDF with OfficeCloud.
Please sign in to view the content.

red_flags.hint: A PDF that holds nothing but a sign-in button is not a contract, it is a disguised login page.
The button leads to officecloud-viewer.test. The real sign-in runs on officecloud.example.

explanation: The sender really is who they claim: the account has probably been taken over. That is why checking the domain does not help here. You have to look at what the PDF actually asks for. If in doubt, call Daniel Roth on the number you already know.

content.subject: Invoice RE-2026-8841 for your order PO-2026-4120
content.body_md:
Dear Sir or Madam,

please find attached the invoice for your order PO-2026-4120. Payment is due within 30 days as agreed.

Please note our new bank details as shown on the invoice.

Kind regards
Kessler Stahl GmbH

red_flags.hint: The real supplier writes from kessler-stahl.example, not kessler-stahl.test. Only the ending changes.
New account details by email are the heart of invoice fraud. Always check through the phone number you already know.
Order number and goods can come from a stolen mailbox. They prove nothing.

explanation: The hardest kind: a real order number, a calm tone, normal payment terms, no link. If you wave this through as "OK", accounting pays the fraudsters. A change of bank details is always a reason to call.

content.subject: Quote for Q1 transport framework – confidential
content.body_md:
Hello,

please find attached our quote for the transport framework in the first quarter. As it contains prices, the file is password protected.

The password is: 4471

Best regards
Sabine Lorenz

red_flags.hint: A password in the same email protects nothing. It has one purpose: virus scanners cannot open and check the file.
A sender you have never dealt with, and a quote you did not ask for.
PDFs can carry malicious code or links as well. The ending .pdf alone does not make a file harmless.

explanation: Encrypted attachments get past the checks on the mail server. Real partners send the password through a second channel, and you know that a quote is coming.

content.subject: Application for purchasing clerk (ref. 2026-117)
content.body_md:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am applying for the position of purchasing clerk advertised on your website. You will find my CV and references attached.

I look forward to hearing from you.

Kind regards
Lena Hartwig

pdf.title: Content cannot be displayed
lines: This document was created with a newer version.
Update your PDF reader to see the CV and references.

red_flags.hint: A document that demands an update almost always brings malware. The link ends in .exe.
Real updates come through IT, never from a job application.

explanation: HR departments have to open attachments from strangers. That is exactly why they are a popular target. Opening the PDF was still fine, clicking "Update" would have been the mistake.

content.subject: Your 2025 tax assessment is ready
content.body_md:
Hello,

a new assessment for the 2025 tax year is available for you. You will find the document attached to this message.

This is an automatically generated email.

pdf.title: Assessment for 2025
lines: So that we can pay out this amount, please confirm your bank details.

red_flags.hint: The real portal is steuerportal.example. "-service.test" belongs to someone else.
The tax office already knows your account. Nobody has to confirm details for a refund through a button in a PDF.

explanation: A real notification has no assessment attached: you sign in to the portal yourself, through your bookmark. Money you are owed makes you careless.

content.subject: Final notice before legal action, ref. 2026/41873
content.body_md:
Dear Sir or Madam,

our client has instructed us to enforce an outstanding claim. You will find the details in the attached letter.

To avoid further costs, we ask for payment within 5 days.

Kind regards
Weber, solicitor

red_flags.hint: A short deadline and a threat of costs: you are meant to pay before you ask questions.
No hint what this is really about: no creditor name, no kind of contract. A real claim can be traced.

explanation: The amount is small on purpose: many people pay to avoid trouble. Check whether you know the contract, and ask the law firm on a number you looked up yourself. No contract, no money.

content.subject: Invoice 2026-3391 for PO-2026-4471
content.body_md:
Hello,

please find attached the invoice for your order PO-2026-4471 of 14 October. Payment terms and bank details are unchanged.

If you have questions, you can reach us as usual on the number you already have.

Kind regards
Bauer Elektrik

pdf.issuer: Bauer Elektrik GmbH · Lange Straße 4 · 08056 Zwickau
pdf.title: Invoice 2026-3391
lines: Bank details unchanged as per framework agreement

explanation: Genuine: a known supplier, the right domain, your order number, unchanged bank details, no pressure and no link. Not every PDF is phishing. A false alarm holds up the invoice here.

content.subject: Change of tax class: form
content.body_md:
Hello,

as discussed on the phone yesterday, here is the form for changing your tax class. Please hand it in at the HR office or upload it in the employee portal.

Best regards
Jana Seidel

pdf.title: Change of tax class
lines: Name, staff number, new tax class

explanation: Genuine: you discussed this form yourself, the domain is yours, the link goes to your own portal, and nobody wants a password by email.

content.subject: Your ticket Zwickau – Leipzig on 12 Nov
content.body_md:
Thank you for your booking earlier. You will find your ticket attached. Please show the code when your ticket is checked.

Have a good trip, RailTix

explanation: Genuine: you booked this trip yourself just now, the domain fits, and the code is only shown to a conductor. It asks you nothing. A QR code in a PDF is not automatically an attack.

content.subject: Mandatory: confirm the new travel policy by Friday
content.body_md:
Dear colleagues,

as announced at the staff meeting, the new travel policy applies from December. Please read it and confirm it by Friday in the intranet. You do not need to sign in through this email, you are already signed in there.

Best regards
Compliance

pdf.title: Travel policy 2027
lines: 1. Book only through the travel portal

explanation: Genuine, although "mandatory" and "by Friday" sound like pressure: it was announced, the domain is yours, the link goes to your own intranet, and no password is requested. Real emails have deadlines too.

content.subject: RE: Costing for project Mosel
content.body_md:
Hi,

here is the updated costing we talked about yesterday. Could you take a look at the material costs by tomorrow morning?

Thanks!
Lena

red_flags.hint: Read from the right: the domain is sharedocs.test. "muster-automotive" in front of it is just a freely chosen prefix.

explanation: Lena's account was taken over and the email continues a real conversation: the sender is right, and so is the tone. The only thing that does not fit is the link destination. Hold your finger on a link before you click it. If in doubt, ask Lena in chat or by phone.

content.subject: Mailbox move this weekend: please check beforehand
content.body_md:
Hello,

this weekend we are moving mailboxes to the new platform. Please check in the portal beforehand whether your mailbox is included, so that no emails get lost.

Your IT Service

red_flags.hint: Look closely: "rnuster" instead of "muster". The letters r and n together look almost like an m.
The link also goes to rnuster-automotive.example, not to your company.

explanation: A homoglyph attack: flawless text, a plausible occasion and a domain that only looks wrong at second glance. Misspelled domains are no beginner's trick. They are hard to see. So report when in doubt.

content.subject: Invitation: annual review, Thu 15:00–15:30
content.body_md:
Thomas Berger has invited you to a meeting.

Annual review
Thursday, 15:00–15:30
Online meeting

To join, please sign in with your company account.

red_flags.hint: Invitations from your calendar come from your company, not from officecloud-meet.test.

red_flags.target: body:please sign in with your company account
red_flags.hint: A meeting does not ask for your company account by email. The annual review is just the bait that makes you curious.

explanation: The topic is well chosen: almost everyone opens an annual review with their boss. Check your calendar instead, or simply ask.

content.subject: Quick question
content.body_md:
Hello,

are you in the office today? I have a small, confidential task for you, but I am in a meeting until noon. Just reply here briefly.

T. Berger
Sent from my phone

red_flags.hint: A sender from your company, but the reply would go to a private mailbox. Tap the sender: it is listed there under "Reply to".
Harmless, no money, no link: the first step only wants to start a conversation. The transfer comes later.

explanation: CEO fraud now usually starts without a demand, so that no filter and no gut feeling kicks in. Whoever replies is already writing to the fraudster. Ask your boss through another channel.

content.subject: Action required: new sign-in method by 30 Nov
content.body_md:
Hello everyone,

as announced in the intranet, we are moving to the new sign-in method by 30 Nov. Please set it up in the portal. It takes five minutes, and we will never ask for your password by email or phone.

Your IT Service

explanation: Genuine, even though "action required" and a deadline sound alarming: it is your domain, the link stays on your domain, the measure was announced, and nobody wants a password. Too much mistrust paralyses IT.

content.subject: Today 3 pm: short staff meeting
content.body_md:
Dear colleagues,

today at 3 pm I would like to give you a brief update on the new major order in hall 3. It will take about twenty minutes.

Thomas Berger

explanation: Genuine: the boss writes briefly and at short notice, but asks for nothing except your presence. No money, no link, no secrecy, no different reply address.

content.subject: New message in your mailbox
content.body_md:
Hello,

there is a new message for you in your online banking. Please sign in as usual to read it.

This email deliberately contains no link.

Your Sparkasse Musterstadt

explanation: Genuine: no link, no deadline and no request for data. You sign in your own way. This is exactly what a clean notification looks like.
